title: 2027-07-28-redwood-console-tracing-request-logs-debugging-walkthrough

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-07-28 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Ortiz (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Desai (AtlasHealth), Tom Walsh (Atlas Platform), Sara Kim (Atlas Security), Evan (observer)

[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, i'm lena from Redwood. we'll do a quick console walkthrough focused on tracing, error analysis and request logs - and then spend time on debugging flows that map to your production incidents. samir and i will tag-team.
[00:12] Priya Desai: great thanks, quick context: we're evaluating options for our patient-facing summarization service. latency needs to be sub-300ms p50 for short prompts, and security team requires private VPC + KMS. we also need clear audit trails for any model outputs.
[00:28] Samir Patel: understood. quick agenda: show tracing UI, trace-to-request linking, request logs ingestion and filters, then a live debugging scenario where we reproduce an error span and show rollback / model-variant fallback. sound good?
[00:39] Tom Walsh: yep. also, curious about how kv cache hits surface in traces - we've seen token cost blowouts with some of our batched endpoints.
[00:48] Samir Patel: good callout, we'll show KV cache metrics and per-span token counts.
[00:56] [00:56] Samir Patel: starting screen share now - this is the Redwood Console, top nav has Tracing, Request Logs, Models, Routes. first, Tracing. you'll see a timeline of spans per request, with service names, model variant, and kernel hints (sometimes gensim or kernel names are fuzzy in transcription).
[01:18] Priya Desai: the span names look a bit different than opentelemetry default - are these auto-mapped?
[01:24] Samir Patel: yeah we ingest OTLP and also map common inference events - kv_cache_lookup, batch_assemble, model_forward, token_emit. mapping rules are in the ingestion docs. sometimes the agent names get normalized, so you might see redwood-infer or rwinfer in traces depending on deployment.
[01:44] [01:44] Samir Patel: here's a trace for a failing request - you can see the model_forward span has a long tail and then an error event. clicking into the span shows the error code, stack-ish message, and a link to the associated request log.
[01:58] Sara Kim: what's stored in the request log? any PII?
[02:03] Samir Patel: default retention removes raw prompt content for hosted customers unless configured. for private/Dedicated you control retention and storage; we support KMS-encrypted logs and can ship to your S3/VPC endpoint. for SOC2 customers we recommend field-level redaction and KMS.
[02:24] Lena Ortiz: and that ties to our compliance pack - we'll share the SOC2 summary and KMS integration guide after the call.
[02:31] [02:31] Priya Desai: good. can we see how request logs are queried? we've got lots of microsecond-level latency spikes that aren't consistent.
[02:41] Samir Patel: sure. switching to Request Logs. you can filter by route, model, client id, status, and also by trace id. there's a quick histogram for response time distribution and then a raw events pane with token-level timings when available.
[03:02] [03:02] Samir Patel: here's an example filter: route=:patient-summarize AND status!=200 shows errors across the last 24h. we can also exclude system retries.
[03:12] Tom Walsh: does the console show batching metrics? like batch size distribution per route?
[03:18] Samir Patel: yes - in Request Logs we show batch_size, batch_wait_ms, and kv_cache_hit boolean. you can pivot to see percentiles for batch_size. for large variance we recommend adjusting max_batch_latency or configuring hot partitions.
[03:36] [03:36] Priya Desai: can we do a live debug? i uploaded a short sample of failing traces to the workspace earlier.
[03:43] Samir Patel: perfect - let's search by trace id you sent. paste it in?
[03:50] Priya Desai: pasted.
[03:52] [03:52] Samir Patel: loading... ok trace shows repeated model_forward retries and a stall during kv_cache_lookup for one node. see these child spans with long db_call timings - could be backend cache miss or a kernel fallback.
[04:08] Priya Desai: the spike correlates to a daily job hitting a new prompt template around 03:00 UTC.
[04:16] Samir Patel: that fits. on the trace we can click 'Related Logs' and open the raw request. here you can see the request payload, model variant used, and token delta. note - raw prompt content is redacted in this demo.
[04:32] [04:32] Samir Patel: another useful view is the 'Span Heatmap' which aggregates error rates by span name. you can quickly see that kv_cache_lookup error rate increased 8x during the job window.
[04:45] Tom Walsh: how do rollouts show up? if we can do canary to a quantized variant, will traces show the variant tags?
[04:54] Samir Patel: yes - model_variant is a first-class tag on traces and request logs. you can filter by model_variant=redwood-alpha-8bit to compare latencies and error rates. our Rollouts feature also attaches the rollout_id to traces so post-mortems can easily correlate with deploys.
[05:12] [05:12] Priya Desai: re: quantization - we're worried about hallucination regressions. can we set quality gates tied to eval prompt sets?
[05:21] Samir Patel: absolutely, Redwood Optimize can tie eval results to rollouts and fail the canary automatically if a quality threshold drops. but for this call we can show trace-based signal: token_entropy and per-request BLEU/ROUGE-like metrics if you upload prompt/eval sets.
[05:40] [05:40] Sara Kim: for private deployment, how does tracing data leave our cluster?
[05:46] Samir Patel: for Private you can keep traces entirely behind your VPC - our control plane will point at your collection endpoint. logs can be pushed to S3 or your SIEM via secure streaming with client-side encryption under your KMS. we do not keep raw prompts unless you enable telemetry sharing.
[06:02] [06:02] Priya Desai: what's the retention granularity? we need 12 months of trace metadata for audits, but only 90 days of full request bodies.
[06:11] Lena Ortiz: we support per-tenant retention policies: you can keep metadata for 12 months and raw bodies for 90 days; cold storage options are available. we'll include retention config in the doc pack.
[06:24] [06:24] Samir Patel: let's demo a debugging flow: reproduce a failing trace, identify root cause, then show remediation - model-variant fallback. I'm going to trigger a synthetic request that simulates the job spike.
[06:36] [06:36] Samir Patel: sending request now - you should see a new trace come in.
[06:40] Priya Desai: i see it, trace id 7b3c...
[06:43] [06:43] Samir Patel: click it - you see a queue_wait span indicating batching delay of 120ms and a model_forward rich span showing a kernel fallback to fp32 (you'll see a kernel hint in the notes). that fallback is what increased latency.
[06:59] Priya Desai: curious why batch wait is so high for only a handful of requests.
[07:05] Samir Patel: that often happens if traffic is bursty and the router pins requests to a small pool; the console shows routing decisions and CPU/GPU utilization per pool. we also have an autoscale configuration - for Dedicated you can set pool cpu/gpu headroom and burst concurrency.
[07:23] [07:23] Tom Walsh: can we configure route affinity? some of our tenants have extremely skewed prompt lengths.
[07:29] Samir Patel: yes, Route policies let you pin by client id or by prompt schema. you can also have a fallback route that uses a cheaper quantized variant.
[07:38] [07:38] Samir Patel: back to the demo - to remediate i can flip the route to the canary variant (quantized) for just 5% of traffic; the console will show rollout progress and compare metrics side-by-side. i'm toggling now.
[07:50] [07:50] Priya Desai: i see the new spans with model_variant=canary-8bit, p50 is slightly worse but p95 improved because of fewer kernel fallbacks?
[08:00] Samir Patel: in this synthetic, yes. you can also set Quality Gates so if hallucination/metric degrades, the rollout automatically aborts.
[08:10] [08:10] Sara Kim: for audit, will we get an immutable record of who flipped the rollout?
[08:15] Samir Patel: yes, audit logs record user, timestamp, rollout id and diff; those are exportable to your SIEM.
[08:23] [08:23] Priya Desai: earlier you mentioned KV cache hits shown on traces - can we get a metric for cost per-request from this data?
[08:30] Samir Patel: we expose token_count, kv_cache_hit, and per-token compute estimates. Redwood Console has a Cost view per-route that uses these signals to estimate unit economics. you can break down cost by model_variant, region, and even by prompt-template.
[08:47] [08:47] Tom Walsh: nice. our ops team will want daily reports of expensive prompts.
[08:52] Samir Patel: exportable alerts and scheduled reports are supported. you can also hook to Slack or PagerDuty for regressions.
[08:59] [08:59] Priya Desai: can we replay requests for debugging? e.g., re-run a request through a different variant without hitting user-facing systems?
[09:06] Samir Patel: yes - Request Replay allows you to take a redacted request payload and re-run against a selected model_variant in a sandboxed environment. breadcrumb links in the trace jump you to a 'Replay' button.
[09:17] [09:17] Priya Desai: that would be very useful. any throttling or safety guard?
[09:22] Samir Patel: replays are rate-limited and do not trigger downstream side-effects by default; they run against a read-only mode or a sandbox dataset.
[09:31] [09:31] Lena Ortiz: quick pause - questions on security/compliance?
[09:35] Sara Kim: yes, SSO and RBAC - we need SAML and role scoping by route and environment.
[09:41] Lena Ortiz: Redwood supports SAML SSO and granular RBAC; we can map roles to route permissions and restrict rollout actions. we'll include a sample RBAC matrix in the doc pack.
[09:54] [09:54] Tom Walsh: another thing: how big are the tracing payloads and what about cost for storing 12 months of metadata?
[10:01] Samir Patel: metadata is compact and priced differently than full request bodies - we can provide a cost estimate based on your expected QPS. part of the POC we'll run the numbers.
[10:12] [10:12] Priya Desai: any known limitations for on-prem GPU kits? we've got a mix of A100 and some older T4s.
[10:19] Samir Patel: runtime adapts kernels by GPU type; older cards may fall back to different kernels which affect latency. for Dedicated/Private we provide a performance profile matrix and recommended fleet mix. we'll include that doc.
[10:34] [10:34] Priya Desai: back to the request log ingestion - do you support structured embeddings or only raw events?
[10:41] Samir Patel: request logs can include structured fields (embedding vectors omitted) and custom tags you add at the SDK level. we store vectors as references if you want to keep costs down.
[10:52] [10:52] Samir Patel: quick demo of searching by error fingerprint - type of error and message similarity. console groups similar errors and surfaces a representative stack. this helps triage recurring issues.
[11:05] Priya Desai: will that work across rollouts? e.g., identify if a new canary increased a particular fingerprint?
[11:11] Samir Patel: yes - fingerprints are tagged with rollout_id and you can pivot error rates vs rollout windows.
[11:20] [11:20] Tom Walsh: our SREs usually want to receive traces in our existing Grafana/Tempo stack - can Redwood output to OTLP?
[11:27] Samir Patel: absolutely - we support OTLP export and you can choose to stream traces to your backend or ours. for Private you probably keep it internal.
[11:36] [11:36] Priya Desai: one more practical - when we run the POC, what telemetry should we send to get the most signal?
[11:42] Samir Patel: send traces with span names we recommend (kv_cache_lookup, model_forward, token_emit), route id, model_variant, batch_size, kv_cache_hit, and a redacted prompt id. also include any downstream db call spans to correlate backend latency.
[11:58] [11:58] Priya Desai: ok i'll work with tom to dump a 48-hour window.
[12:02] [12:02] Samir Patel: perfect - i noted the trace ids you pasted earlier.
[12:07] [12:07] Lena Ortiz: quick recap and next steps: lena to send SOC2 + KMS docs; samir will run the request-log demo with their sample logs and share screenshots; priya to share redacted 48h logs; we schedule POC kickoff for week of 2027-08-09. sound right?
[12:25] Priya Desai: yes, thank you both. this was helpful - showed exactly what we'd need for debugging flows.
[12:32] Tom Walsh: appreciate the rollout demo and replay feature. will look for the docs.
[12:36] Sara Kim: thanks, prioritizing security review once we see the SOC2 pack.
[12:40] Samir Patel: thanks everyone - we'll follow up with the doc bundle and Doodle for POC scheduling.
[12:48] Lena Ortiz: thanks all, talk soon.

[End of transcript]

Notes on transcription quality: medium - occasional normalization of product names (rwinfer instead of Redwood Infer), and a few audio cuts during live demo. Some technical terms transcribed imperfectly (e.g., kernel fallback spelled out as "fp32 fallback" but audio said "fall back to fp three too").
